My goal is to create a calm and positive dental experience for every child. Palm Valley Pediatric Dentistry & Orthodontics provides dental care for infants, children, and teens, including preventive exams, cleanings, fluoride treatments, dental sealants, restorative and orthodontic care, and emergency dental care. My team and I use child-friendly, age-appropriate techniques to help children maintain healthy teeth and gums at every stage. We help children develop good oral hygiene habits while caring for common pediatric dental concerns such as cavities, tooth decay, dental emergencies, and bite or tooth alignment issues. New Patients Welcome Same-Day Emergency Appointments Schedule Your Child’s Visit Today Dr. Olga Dolghier at Palm Valley Dental Office in Scottsdale, AZ Specialized Pediatric Dental Care Every child develops differently, and some dental needs require more than routine preventive visits. We offer focused care for tongue-tie concerns, airway development, tooth extractions, and children who need additional support during dental treatment. Our team considers each child’s development and individual needs when planning care. Orthodontic Care As children grow, changes in tooth position can affect how their teeth meet and function together. Our orthodontic care addresses concerns such as crowding, spacing, crooked teeth, overbites, and underbites. We use braces when appropriate to improve tooth position and bite alignment as children grow. Invisalign Clear Aligners For suitable teens and adults, Invisalign clear aligners offer a discreet way to improve tooth position and address certain bite problems. The removable trays make it easy to eat, brush, and floss as usual. Invisalign can gradually straighten crooked teeth, close gaps, and improve certain alignment concerns for a more balanced, confident smile. Meet Dr. Olga Dolghier As the owner and founder of Palm Valley Pediatric Dentistry & Orthodontics, Dr. Olga Dolghier is a Diplomate of the American Board of Pediatric Dentistry with more than 15 years of experience. She stays current through continuing education and incorporates evidence-based approaches and emerging technologies into pediatric dental care. Dr. Olga helps parents understand their child’s dental care options so they can make informed decisions with confidence. She also builds lasting relationships with families as their child grows. Schedule With Dr. Olga Our Pediatric Dentistry Services for Growing Smiles We have created a warm and playful space where kids can feel relaxed and parents can feel good about their child’s care. Routine Checkups & Cleanings Kids smile a lot, and we love helping keep those smiles bright. During checkups, we gently clean teeth, remove plaque, and check for any early signs of cavities or other concerns. We also teach fun, simple brushing and flossing habits so children can take great care of their teeth at home. Read More Show Less Cavity Fillings & Preventive Care If your child has a cavity, we use tooth-colored fillings that look natural and blend right in. We offer dental sealants to help protect back teeth from decay. Preventive dental care is a big part of keeping little smiles healthy. Read More Show Less Baby’s First Dental Visit Your baby’s first dental visit happens around the first birthday or when the first tooth appears. At this visit, we examine your baby’s mouth, clean the teeth if needed, and share easy care tips. Parents get guidance on teething, thumb-sucking, pacifier use, and making brushing fun from the start. Read More Show Less Braces & Invisalign When it is time to straighten your child’s teeth, we offer braces and Invisalign clear aligners. We look at your child’s smile, bite, and growth to recommend the best option. Some children may start seeing changes in as little as 6 to 12 months. Read More Show Less Tongue-Tie & Lip-Tie Laser Treatments Some babies and children have tongue-ties or lip-ties that can affect feeding, speech, oral development, or brushing. We use a gentle CO₂ laser to perform safe releases in just a short visit.  Read More Show Less Sedation & Special Care Some children feel extra nervous at the dentist or need help staying calm during longer treatments. We offer safe sedation options to help children feel relaxed and comfortable during care. We also provide support for children with special healthcare needs. Read More Show Less Airway Obstruction Snoring, restless sleep, and teeth grinding can sometimes point to airway problems. Our pediatric dental team can check for the signs of airway obstruction and help guide treatment that supports better breathing, better sleep, and healthier development. Read More Show Less In-Office Sedation Dental visits should feel manageable, not scary. Our in-office sedation services help children stay calm and comfortable during treatment without visiting another facility. It is one more way we make care easier for families. Read More Show Less Advanced Technology for Better Dental Care Modern technology provides detailed information to support diagnostic and treatment decisions. These tools help us evaluate dental needs and plan care with greater precision and efficiency. iTero® Digital Scanners Our iTero digital scanners create detailed 3D images of your child’s teeth. These images support orthodontic planning, Invisalign treatment, and progress monitoring. Low-Radiation Digital X-Rays Digital X-rays provide clear images of teeth and surrounding structures with low radiation exposure. They can also reveal concerns that may not be visible during a routine exam. Laser Dentistry We use dental laser technology for certain soft-tissue procedures, including tongue-tie release and lip-tie treatment. It can help minimize bleeding and may reduce the need for sutures in appropriate cases. Kerr™ Composite Fillings Kerr composite materials provide tooth-colored restorations that blend naturally with surrounding teeth. They offer a conservative option for restoring damaged teeth while maintaining a natural-looking smile. Book Appointment Pediatric Dentistry and Orthodontics Near You! Accepting New Patients Palm Valley Pediatric Dentistry proudly welcomes new patients to our Scottsdale office and all Arizona locations. Families continue choosing our team because they trust us for gentle care, expert treatment, and a child-focused approach. Your Child’s Happy Smile is our Motivation! First tooth? First braces? Great oral health starts early and grows with care. That’s why we focus on building real trust with every child and family we see. When kids feel safe at the dentist, they actually want to come back and that makes all the difference for their long-term dental health. Why Palm Valley for Your Child? Bring your child in, we will take a look, and we will give you honest and zero-pressure guidance on the best path forward. Easy as that. In-House Discount Programs Skip the insurance headache. This encounter can significantly influence your child’s perspective on dental care, setting the tone for a life of proper oral health and care. GET In TOUCH Pediatric Dentistry includes assessing tooth development,  and assessing the health of teeth that are present in the mouth.  Pediatric Dentists are also trained to provide care for children with complex medical histories, behavioral health conditions, and special circumstances.   Our goal is to set the foundation for a lifetime of healthy teeth and healthy habits. Our office  will guide you through preparing for your child’s first pediatric dentist appointment, including what to expect during the visit, how to deal with dental anxiety, and the steps to follow afterwards for optimal home care. What Happens During the Visit Arrival: Checking In and Waiting Room When arriving at the office, you will be greeted by a member of our team who will assist you with checking in your child for their appointment. The waiting room has plenty of options to keep your little one entertained so they don’t feel anxious about their upcoming appointment.  The waiting rooms also have plenty of reading materials for parents to enjoy while they wait. Initial Examination: Checking Teeth, Gums, and Jaw Once you and your child are called, you will have the option to accompany them throughout the entire process. We believe parents know their children best and we welcome your presence for the initial exam.  The Doctor will perform a thorough examination of your child’s teeth, gums, and mouth.. This includes checking each tooth for cavities, damage, and assessing potential bite alignment issues. The dentist will also examine your child’s gum health, which is crucial as healthy gums provide support and protect against bacteria Doctor Review: X-Rays and Structural Assessment X-rays play a critical role in pediatric dentistry, allowing the dentist to see between teeth where cavities often start and beneath the gums to find cavities that are not visible directly. X-rays also allow the Doctor to evaluate the growth and development of permanent teeth including if there is sufficient space for the permanent teeth to erupt in the future.    X-rays are the standard of care in Pediatric Dentistry and Orthodontics for these reasons. Cleaning and Preventive Care: Importance of Regular Checkups The visit includes cleaning your child’s teeth to remove any plaque or tartar buildup with  specialized tools for children to ensure their comfort.  Regular dental check-ups are essential for maintaining good oral hygiene and preventing cavities.  Regular dental check-ups are also essential in identifying cavities before they cause pain or infection. The Doctor may recommend fluoride application for strengthening teeth and preventing cavities. Education and Guidance: Oral Hygiene Tips for Kids In addition to the physical examination and treatment, the pediatric dentist will spend time educating both of you on proper brushing techniques and overall oral hygiene practices. This includes advice on how to brush effectively, the importance of flossing, and tips on maintaining a healthy diet to support dental health. This guidance is tailored to help you foster good dental habits at home from an early age to ensure optimal dental care throughout life.  Play Dealing with Dental Anxiety: Tips for Parents and Caregivers Creating a Positive Pre-Visit Narrative To help your child feel more comfortable about their upcoming dental visit, our Doctors  recommend discussing the visit with your child as early as possible. Introduce the concept of the dentist in a fun and engaging way by focusing on the positive aspects. Explain the visit using simple, positive language and avoid sharing any negative experiences. This approach helps in building trust and reducing fear associated with the unknown. You can also enhance this process by reading childrens’ books about dental visits or playing games that involve dental care, making the idea of visiting the dentist familiar and less intimidating. As a parent, you have the ability to stay with them during the entire visit to provide encouragement and positive affirmations. Techniques to Alleviate Fear: Games and Visualization Incorporating playful and interactive techniques can significantly reduce dental anxiety in children. Before the visit, you can use the Tell-Show-Play-doh technique, where children are shown dental tools using Play-doh. to familiarize themselves with the instruments in a non-threatening way.  Additionally, smartphone dentist games that simulate dental procedures through animated visuals and sounds can provide a first-hand experience of what to expect during the visit to also help ease anxiety. Role of Pediatric Dental Staff in Easing Child’s Fears The pediatric dental staff plays a crucial role in managing your child’s dental anxiety. The team at PVPD is trained to use age-appropriate language and to explain dental procedures in a way that is easy for children to understand.  The pediatric dentists will explain a procedure and demonstrate it on a model before performing it; this helps children to know exactly what to expect. Additionally, the dental office environment is designed to be child-friendly, featuring special chairs and playful artwork tailored for children to create a welcoming and less intimidating atmosphere. After the Visit: Next Steps and Home Care Follow-Up Appointments and Treatments as Needed After your child’s dental visit, the PVPD team may schedule follow-up appointments to monitor progress or address any additional dental needs. It’s crucial to keep these appointments to ensure your child’s dental health remains on track. If further treatments such as fillings, sealants, or orthodontic referrals are required, staying timely with these treatments is essential for preventing more complex dental issues from developing. Implementing Oral Care Routine at Home To maintain your child’s dental health, consistent home care routines are vital. You should brush your child’s teeth twice a day using a fluoride toothpaste and soft-bristled toothbrush. For younger children, you will need to assist or complete the brushing to ensure proper technique and thoroughness. Flossing daily is also crucial once your child has teeth that touch.  Children do not have adequate dexterity to maintain their oral hygiene until they are able to tie their own shoe laces.  Parents should plan to assist with brushing through the first ten years of age. Importance of Regular Dental Visits for Ongoing Health Regular dental checkups are not just for addressing immediate dental issues but are also essential for preventing potential problems before they become serious. These visits allow the dentist to catch early signs of tooth decay, monitor the development of your child’s teeth, and provide preventive treatments like fluoride applications to strengthen tooth enamel. Ensuring your child visits the dentist regularly, typically every six months, is a proactive step towards maintaining a healthy smile and promoting overall dental health. Regular check-ins with the dentist also help your child build a positive relationship with dental care providers, making future visits less daunting Call to book An Appointment FAQS What occurs at the beginning of a dental examination for a new patient? At the start of a dental examination for a new patient, the dentist begins with an initial consultation and reviews the patient’s oral medical history. Following this, a comprehensive dental exam is conducted and necessary x-rays are taken to assess the overall oral health of the patient. Can cavities be filled during the initial dental visit? Yes, during the first dental visit, aside from other procedures like teeth cleaning, cavities may also be filled if necessary. What are the typical procedures during a routine dental visit? During a routine dental visit, after cleaning your child’s teeth, the dentist will perform a quick check-up of your teeth, examine your gums, soft palate, throat, neck, and look for any abnormalities. Additionally, any x-rays taken will be reviewed.
